headline: QuantaCoin Cascade Wipes 9 Billion Quanta in 36 Hours
body:
QuantaCoin, the decentralized quanta-adjacent cryptocurrency that had captured nearly 18 percent of informal savings accounts in The Shelf and The Narrows over the past four years, collapsed in a catastrophic de-peg event beginning at 0200 hours Tuesday. By the time Meridian's primary exchanges suspended trading thirty-six hours later, an estimated 9.1 billion quanta in equivalent value had been wiped from approximately 3.4 million holders. The trigger appears to be a coordinated sell-pressure attack — market analysts at Sterling-Nakamura's trading desk identified seventeen simultaneous whale-wallet liquidations, each exceeding 40 million quanta in value, executed within a four-minute window. Whether those wallets are connected to a single actor remains unknown.

For millions of residents in lower-district housing blocks, QuantaCoin was not a speculative asset — it was a primary savings vehicle, chosen because it operated outside Axiom and Tessera's locked wage-escrow systems. 'I had 6,200 quanta in QC. That was two years of extra shifts,' said Benedikt Solano-Okoye, a maintenance worker from The Shelf's Block 44. 'This morning it's worth 190 quanta. How do I explain that to my kids?' The Shelf Voice has catalogued over 900 similar accounts in a community survey posted this morning. The Collective estimates that affected households in The Narrows alone lost a combined 340 million quanta in savings.

The Graycloaks information brokerage network has already begun selling dossiers purporting to identify the coordinated wallet addresses, with pricing starting at 500 quanta per packet. Multiple sources inside the Federal Remnant's Financial Stability Bureau confirm an investigation is open, but the bureau has no jurisdiction over fully decentralized instruments. Ringo Corporation, which operated several licensed QuantaCoin exchange nodes, has quietly delisted the asset and issued a statement emphasizing that node operators 'bear no liability for underlying asset performance.'

The Underground Signal is reporting unconfirmed claims that the Graycloaks have traced at least three of the whale wallets to shell accounts registered through Ironclad subsidiaries — a charge Ironclad has denied in blunt terms. The Sterling-Nakamura Quanta Stability Index fell 2.3 points on the news, its steepest single-session drop in eighteen months.
aftermath: A Federal Remnant inquiry concluded fourteen months later that the collapse was definitively orchestrated but declined to name responsible parties, citing jurisdictional limits — a ruling The Underground Signal called 'the most expensive non-answer in Meridian history.'
runner_relevance: The collapse generated a surge in data-retrieval and investigation contracts almost immediately — affected community groups, The Collective, and anonymous wealthy clients all posted work seeking wallet trace data, exchange node logs, and internal Ringo communications. Runners with financial-system intrusion skills commanded 12,000–20,000 quanta per successful data pull. Simultaneously, the desperation of newly impoverished residents created a buyer's market for runners willing to take low-pay courier and smuggling work, and several criminal contractors — including Iron Lotus cells — began aggressive recruitment of newly broke former savers as low-level operatives, with runners hired to vet and sometimes abduct high-value recruits.
